summary:
Implemented the Tabs feature in the repository, but nothing was run: the work was done by reading and editing files only, as instructed, so the new tests and the Opacity change are unverified.

Changes:
- src/textual/widgets/tabs.py (new): Tab, TabsRenderable, and Tabs. TabsRenderable does the width arithmetic through layout_resolve and builds the label row and underline. Tabs holds state, keyboard handling, and the animation watcher. Only Tab and Tabs are exported; the package __init__ is untouched.
- src/textual/renderables/underline_bar.py: clickable_ranges input (fifth position is width). Yields one Text with click spans applied last, none on the zero-width early path.
- src/textual/renderables/opacity.py: blended style merged with style + blended so other attributes and meta are kept.
- tests/renderables/test_underline_bar.py: new cases. tests/widgets/test_tabs.py and tests/widgets/__init__.py are new.
- docs/reference/tabs.md and sandbox/tabs_demo.py are new.

Open issues:
- Layout resolver: no change. Edge already has size, min_size (default 1), and fraction, and the resolver already uses min_size.
- Spec conflict: the bar starts at the find_tab_by_name index (full list), but is rendered over displayed tabs. With duplicate names ahead of the active tab, the underline can land on the wrong tab. I followed the spec literally and did not fix it.
- An empty label has size 0, which the resolver treats as flexible, so it gets a one-cell slot.
- Choices not covered by the spec: Tabs.can_focus = True; letter search only for single-character keys; click action built with repr(name) so ordinary names keep single quotes.
- Unverified: constructing Tabs in tests may need a running app because reactive watchers post messages; the tests read private reactive attributes; Opacity meta preservation assumes rich's Style addition keeps meta when the added style has none.
- Commits: none made.
